newsitem.title: USA: Northwestern Public Service adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Northwestern Public Service adopts rights plan.

text.p: Northwestern Public Service said Tuesday its board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan.
The energy company said the plan was not in response to any specific takeover attempt.

"The plan is not designed to prevent a takeover, but provides additional flexibility to our board in responding to the negative effects of abusive share accumulation tactics such as 'greenmail' and 'two-tier' takeover attempts and tender offers that do not offer an adequate price to all shareholders," chief executive officer Merle Lewis said in a statement.
The plan would be triggered under certain circumstances, including the acquisition by any person or group of 15 percent or more of the company's common stock.
Northwestern Power shares fell 3/8 to 35 Tuesday.
